video.title: The TOP 25 Players In Fantasy Basketball [Cats & Points]

summary: Josh Lloyd gives his top 25 fantasy basketball rankings as of September 16, 2026, for Yahoo points, ESPN points, head-to-head 9-category and 8-category roto leagues. He stresses that the gaps between players are small, especially from picks 5 to 20. Nikola Jokic is his number one in Yahoo points and categories, and Victor Wembanyama is number one in ESPN points. He shares data showing about 37% of the top 25 turns over each season, and most players who drop out do so because of missed games, not worse play. In 9-cat he is lower than consensus on Cade Cunningham, Jalen Johnson, Tyrese Maxey and Tyrese Haliburton. He ranks Anthony Edwards, Kevin Durant, Amen Thompson and Austin Reaves higher than consensus. He ends with how much injury concerns cost players like Kawhi Leonard, Joel Embiid, Kyrie Irving, Anthony Davis and Stephen Curry.

rules.text: Differences between first-round players are marginal. Picking order in round one rarely wins or loses a league. Unexpected injuries do.
rules.quote: It's not it's not the thing that wins or loses. Unexpected injuries that'll lose your league.

rules.text: A pick is only clearly too early when six or seven players who fit that spot better are still available.
rules.quote: if I see six, seven players that I think might be better suited than that player in that area

rules.text: In points leagues, the biggest drivers of fantasy points are usage and minutes.
rules.quote: because the biggest driver of fantasy points is usage and minutes.

rules.text: Over five seasons, about 37% of the qualified 9-cat top 25 changed from one year to the next. About 16 of 25 repeat.
75% of top 10 players stay inside the top 25 the next year. Players who stay in the top 25 move about five spots on average, with a median of four.
rules.quote: The top 10 players, 75% of those guys remain as top 25 players.

rules.text: 54% of top 25 exits came from players missing the 50 game or 1500 minute threshold because of injury, not from playing worse. Availability is the biggest threat.
rules.quote: 54% of them in fact were not due to them being bad.

rules.text: Every top 25 player who stayed eligible but dropped out of the top 25 still finished top 50. Healthy top 25 players do not bottom out.
rules.quote: every player who remained eligible but did drop out of the top 25, they still were top 50 players.

rules.text: In head-to-head, efficiency is the most variable category week to week. He prefers consistent volume over a small efficiency edge.
rules.quote: efficiency is the most variable thing week on week, game by game.

rules.text: Usage strongly correlates with points-league value but correlates much less with category-league success.
rules.quote: usage doesn't correlate to fantasy category success as much as it does in points leagues.

rules.text: A star joining a new team tends to lose some value.
rules.quote: Big Star joining a new team is an impact thing. It it does have a it does have a decrease in value.

rules.text: Draft players knowing their strengths and weaknesses. A weak category like free throws is acceptable.
rules.quote: You know, when you draft what a player's strengths and weaknesses are. That's okay.

rules.text: In competitive roto, you can win while punting a category. Punting becomes more viable with more teams, more categories and deeper leagues.
rules.quote: The more competitive, the more teams, the more categories, the more viable punting a category is.

rules.text: Injuries matter less in roto than in head-to-head.
rules.quote: At number 11, injuries don't factor as much in this format.

rules.text: Rankings are ordinal, not value gaps. Number 6 is not much better than 8 or 12. Adjust picks based on your earlier picks.
rules.quote: Six is not that much better than 8, not that much better than 12th
